Perfect. We're going to build a **custom Daily & Session Range Box indicator for MNQ on the 5-minute chart**, using Momo's own coding language.

Here's how I understand the indicator you want.

### 1. Daily Range Box

For each trading day, the indicator will automatically draw a rectangle around all the 5-minute candles.

- **Left boundary:** The first 5-minute candle of the trading day.
- **Right boundary:** The last 5-minute candle of that day.
- **Top boundary:** The highest wick reached during the day.
- **Bottom boundary:** The lowest wick reached during the day.

The rectangle should update dynamically as new candles form, then remain fixed once the trading day ends.

### 2. Session Range Boxes

We'll apply the same logic to individual trading sessions, potentially including:

- Asian session
- London session
- New York session

Each session can have its own color, boundaries, and visibility settings.

### 3. Indicator settings

Ideally, we'll make these customizable:

| Setting | Function |
|---|---|
| Daily Box | Show/hide daily rectangles |
| Session Boxes | Show/hide individual sessions |
| Box Color | Separate color for each session |
| Border Thickness | Adjust outline width |
| Fill Opacity | Transparent background inside rectangles |
| Historical Boxes | Display previous days and sessions |
| Session Times | Customize start and end times |

**One important detail:** MNQ futures trade nearly 24 hours, so we'll need to distinguish the full futures trading day from the regular New York market session.

### ASSISTANT 2026-10-17 06:19
Here's the **Mai Language code for moomoo**, designed for the MNQ 5-minute chart. It includes three range boxes: the full futures trading day, London, and New York. No Asian session.

The default times are Eastern Time (Montreal/New York).

| Box | Start | End | Color |
|---|---|---|---|
| Daily (CME) | 6:00 PM | 5:00 PM next day | Gray |
| London | 3:00 AM | 11:30 AM | Magenta |
| New York | 9:30 AM | 4:00 PM | Yellow |

## Mai Language code


{MNQ DAILY + LONDON + NEW YORK RANGE BOXES}
{Designed for 5-minute candles}
{Times assume Eastern Time}

{========== DAILY FUTURES SESSION ==========}

D_IN:=TIME>=1800 OR TIME<1700;
D_START:=TIME=1800;
D_END:=D_IN AND (TIME=1655 OR ISLASTBAR);

D_BARS:=BARSLAST(D_START)+1;
D_HI:=HHV(H,D_BARS);
D_LO:=LLV(L,D_BARS);

D_NEXT:=BARSNEXT(D_END);
D_TOP:=REFX(D_HI,D_NEXT);
D_BOT:=REFX(D_LO,D_NEXT);

DAILY_HIGH:IF(D_IN,D_TOP,DRAWNULL),COLORGRAY,DOTLINE;
DAILY_LOW:IF(D_IN,D_BOT,DRAWNULL),COLORGRAY,DOTLINE;

STICKLINE(D_START,D_TOP,D_BOT,0,0),COLORGRAY;
STICKLINE(D_END,D_TOP,D_BOT,0,0),COLORGRAY;


{========== LONDON SESSION ==========}

L_IN:=TIME>=300 AND TIME<1130;
L_START:=L_IN AND REF(L_IN,1)=0;
L_END:=L_IN AND (TIME=1125 OR ISLASTBAR);

L_BARS:=BARSLAST(L_START)+1;
L_HI:=HHV(H,L_BARS);
L_LO:=LLV(L,L_BARS);

L_NEXT:=BARSNEXT(L_END);
L_TOP:=REFX(L_HI,L_NEXT);
L_BOT:=REFX(L_LO,L_NEXT);

LONDON_HIGH:IF(L_IN,L_TOP,DRAWNULL),COLORMAGENTA,DOTLINE;
LONDON_LOW:IF(L_IN,L_BOT,DRAWNULL),COLORMAGENTA,DOTLINE;

STICKLINE(L_START,L_TOP,L_BOT,0,0),COLORMAGENTA;
STICKLINE(L_END,L_TOP,L_BOT,0,0),COLORMAGENTA;

DRAWTEXT(L_START,L_TOP*1.0005,'LONDON'),COLORMAGENTA;


{========== NEW YORK SESSION ==========}

N_IN:=TIME>=930 AND TIME<1600;
N_START:=N_IN AND REF(N_IN,1)=0;
N_END:=N_IN AND (TIME=1555 OR ISLASTBAR);

N_BARS:=BARSLAST(N_START)+1;
N_HI:=HHV(H,N_BARS);
N_LO:=LLV(L,N_BARS);

N_NEXT:=BARSNEXT(N_END);
N_TOP:=REFX(N_HI,N_NEXT);
N_BOT:=REFX(N_LO,N_NEXT);

NY_HIGH:IF(N_IN,N_TOP,DRAWNULL),COLORYELLOW,DOTLINE;
NY_LOW:IF(N_IN,N_BOT,DRAWNULL),COLORYELLOW,DOTLINE;

STICKLINE(N_START,N_TOP,N_BOT,0,0),COLORYELLOW;
STICKLINE(N_END,N_TOP,N_BOT,0,0),COLORYELLOW;

DRAWTEXT(N_START,N_TOP*1.0005,'NEW YORK'),COLORYELLOW;


## How to install

In your moomoo indicator editor:

1. Select **Mai Language**.
2. Set Symbol to `MNQBOX` and Name to `MNQ Daily & Session Boxes`.
3. Set **Exhibition Area → Main**.
4. Paste the code, leave Parameter Settings empty, and click **Apply**.
5. Open your MNQ chart on the **5-minute timeframe**.

Moomoo documents the Mai Language editor and its plotting syntax, including `IF`, drawing functions, and line colors. <Cite ref="turn658241search0"/>

**Important:** This is a first version and has not been compiled in your installation. It uses `BARSNEXT` and `REFX` to look ahead within loaded chart data, allowing historical boxes to display their completed high/low ranges. These are future-looking functions, so the shapes can update while a session is developing. The clock times also assume that moomoo's chart timestamps are Eastern Time; London hours can shift relative to New York during the brief daylight-saving transition periods.

Paste it into moomoo and click **Apply**. If you get a compilation error, send me a screenshot showing the error and line number so I can correct the exact syntax.

The critical change is:

```text
D_END:=D_IN AND
       (REFX(D_START,1) OR ISLASTBAR);
```

This should identify the last available candle immediately before the following futures session begins, even if there isn't a candle with the exact expected closing timestamp.

- Start on the first available candle at or after 6:00 PM ET.
- Include overnight price action, London, and New York.
- Capture the full high and low of all candles in that trading day.
- Finish at the last candle before the next trading session.
- Update while the current trading day is forming.

### Why this should work differently

Instead of detecting the day solely from the previous candle's time, `D_KEY` remembers the date of the most recent evening trading session. That same identifier carries through midnight until the following evening.

The rectangle then uses the highest and lowest prices from that group of candles.

NY_LOW:IF(N_IN,N_BOT,DRAWNULL),COLORYELLOW,DOTLINE;

## What it would display


  <AsyncImage query="trading candlestick chart higher high HH lower high LH higher low HL lower low LL market structure labels diagram dark background" aspectRatio="16:9" width="100%"/>


| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| HH | Higher High — new swing high above the previous one |
| LH | Lower High — new swing high below the previous one |
| HL | Higher Low — new swing low above the previous one |
| LL | Lower Low — new swing low below the previous one |

### Option 1 — Look for an existing indicator

In moomoo desktop, open your indicator manager and search for `ZigZag`, `Fractal`, or `Swing`.

There's also a community-created <Link url="https://www.moomoo.com/community/feed/fractals-zigzag-indicator-114588363456518" title="Fractals ZigZag indicator for moomoo"/> that identifies swing highs and lows. <Cite ref="turn153918search2"/>

It may not label all four structures automatically, but it's worth checking first.

### Option 2 — Build our own for MNQ

We can use the same Mai Language editor we used for your Daily, London, and New York rectangles.

I would recommend building it as a **separate indicator**, with labels directly above and below the 5-minute candles.

There's one important distinction: a swing high or low can only be *confirmed* after subsequent price action. For example, requiring two candles on the right of a potential swing means confirmation comes at least 10 minutes later on your 5-minute chart. Earlier signals are possible, but they can change as new candles form.

We're going to create a **separate Market Structure indicator for MNQ**, using moomoo's Mai Language. It will identify confirmed swing highs and lows and automatically label them HH, LH, HL, or LL.

## 1. Complete Mai Language code


{MNQ MARKET STRUCTURE V1}
{CONFIRMED HH LH HL LL}
{5 MINUTE CHART}
{2 LEFT + 2 RIGHT CANDLES}

{========== CONFIRMED SWING POINTS ==========}

P_H:=REF(H,2)>REF(H,3) AND REF(H,2)>REF(H,4) AND REF(H,2)>REF(H,1) AND REF(H,2)>H;

P_L:=REF(L,2)<REF(L,3) AND REF(L,2)<REF(L,4) AND REF(L,2)<REF(L,1) AND REF(L,2)<L;

{========== SWING PRICES ==========}

S_H:=REF(H,2);
S_L:=REF(L,2);

{========== PREVIOUS SWING PRICES ==========}

PR_H:=REF(VALUEWHEN(P_H,S_H),1);
PR_L:=REF(VALUEWHEN(P_L,S_L),1);

{========== ENSURE PREVIOUS SWING EXISTS ==========}

H_OK:=COUNT(P_H,0)>=2;
L_OK:=COUNT(P_L,0)>=2;

{========== MARKET STRUCTURE ==========}

HH_SIG:=P_H AND H_OK AND S_H>PR_H;
LH_SIG:=P_H AND H_OK AND S_H<PR_H;

HL_SIG:=P_L AND L_OK AND S_L>PR_L;
LL_SIG:=P_L AND L_OK AND S_L<PR_L;

{========== DRAW LABELS AT SWING CANDLES ==========}

DRAWTEXT(REFX(HH_SIG,2),H*1.0004,'HH'),COLORLIGREEN;

DRAWTEXT(REFX(LH_SIG,2),H*1.0004,'LH'),COLORLIRED;

DRAWTEXT(REFX(HL_SIG,2),L*0.9996,'HL'),COLORLIGREEN;

DRAWTEXT(REFX(LL_SIG,2),L*0.9996,'LL'),COLORLIRED;

The indicator compares each confirmed swing high with the previous confirmed swing high, and each confirmed swing low with the previous confirmed swing low. Equal highs or lows are left unlabeled.

On your 5-minute MNQ chart, confirmation happens **10 minutes after the pivot candle closes**. The label is then placed back on the actual pivot candle using `REFX`.

This means the label appears retrospectively; it was not known at the pivot candle itself. Once the confirmation candle has closed, that swing classification is based on completed candles.

LH_SIG:=PH AND PREVH>0 AND CH<PREVH;

{========== ACTIVE STRUCTURE LEVELS ==========}

HIGH_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PH,CH);
LOW_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PL,CL);

{========== BREAK OF STRUCTURE ==========}

BOS_UP:=HIGH_LEVEL>0 AND C>HIGH_LEVEL AND REF(C,1)<=REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1);

BOS_DN:=LOW_LEVEL>0 AND C<LOW_LEVEL AND REF(C,1)>=REF(LOW_LEVEL,1);

{========== BOS LABELS ==========}

DRAWTEXT(BOS_UP,HIGH_LEVEL+8,'BOS'),COLORYELLOW;

DRAWTEXT(BOS_DN,LOW_LEVEL-8,'BOS'),COLORYELLOW;


### How BOS is detected

- **Bullish BOS:** A 5-minute candle closes above the most recent confirmed swing high.
- **Bearish BOS:** A 5-minute candle closes below the most recent confirmed swing low.
- **Dotted line:** Connects the swing level to the breakout candle.
- **BOS label:** Appears near the price level that was broken.

This uses `DRAWLINE` and `DRAWTEXT`, which are available in Mai Language's drawing-function list. The line styling and complete code have not yet been tested inside your moomoo editor. <Cite ref="turn964188search0"/> <Cite ref="turn964188search3"/>

A couple of distinctions matter: this version detects breaks of the latest confirmed swing levels, so it may signal another BOS if price crosses the same level again. It also does not yet distinguish BOS from **CHoCH (Change of Character)**, which appears in your reference.

Try replacing `MNQMS` with V3 and clicking **Apply**. If the BOS lines appear correctly, the next refinement would be to distinguish trend-continuation BOS from reversal CHoCH and prevent repeated breaks of the same swing level.

{MNQ MARKET STRUCTURE V4}
{HH LH HL LL + BOS + CHOCH}
{MNQ 5 MINUTE CHART}

{========== CONFIRMED SWINGS ==========}

PH:=REF(H,2)=HHV(H,5) AND REF(H,2)>REF(H,3) AND REF(H,2)>REF(H,1) AND NOT(ISLASTBAR);

PL:=REF(L,2)=LLV(L,5) AND REF(L,2)<REF(L,3) AND REF(L,2)<REF(L,1) AND NOT(ISLASTBAR);

CL:=REF(L,2);

{========== PREVIOUS SWINGS ==========}

PREVH:=REF(VALUEWHEN(PH,CH),1);
PREVL:=REF(VALUEWHEN(PL,CL),1);

{========== STRUCTURE CLASSIFICATION ==========}

HH_SIG:=PH AND PREVH>0 AND CH>PREVH;
LH_SIG:=PH AND PREVH>0 AND CH<PREVH;

HL_SIG:=PL AND PREVL>0 AND CL>PREVL;
LL_SIG:=PL AND PREVL>0 AND CL<PREVL;

{========== SWING LABELS ==========}

DRAWTEXT(REFX(HH_SIG,2),H+15,'HH'),COLORWHITE;
DRAWTEXT(REFX(LH_SIG,2),H+15,'LH'),COLORWHITE;

DRAWTEXT(REFX(HL_SIG,2),L-15,'HL'),COLORWHITE;
DRAWTEXT(REFX(LL_SIG,2),L-15,'LL'),COLORWHITE;

{========== ACTIVE STRUCTURE LEVELS ==========}

HIGH_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PH,CH);
LOW_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PL,CL);

{========== FIRST BREAK OF EACH LEVEL ==========}

DN_BREAK:=LOW_LEVEL>0 AND C<LOW_LEVEL AND COUNT(C<LOW_LEVEL,BARSLAST(PL)+1)=1 AND NOT(ISLASTBAR);

OLD_DIR:=REF(VALUEWHEN(UP_BREAK OR DN_BREAK,IF(UP_BREAK,1,-1)),1);

BOS_DN:=DN_BREAK AND OLD_DIR<>1;

CHOCH_DN:=DN_BREAK AND OLD_DIR=1;

## MNQ Opening Swing Points — V1

This will be a **separate indicator** from your existing Market Structure and Daily/Session Boxes indicators.

It identifies confirmed pre-market swing points, carries the latest confirmed pre-market swing levels into the New York open, and identifies new swings during the opening hour.

| Feature | Time (Eastern) | Display |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-market swings | 4:00–9:30 AM | Cyan PMH / PML |
| Opening swings | 9:30–10:30 AM | Green OH / Red OL |
| Pre-market reference levels | 9:30–10:30 AM | Solid horizontal lines |

### Complete Mai Language code


{MNQ OPENING SWING POINTS V1}
{PREMARKET + NEW YORK OPEN}
{5 MINUTE CHART - EASTERN TIME}

{========== SESSION TIMES ==========}

PM_IN:=TIME>=400 AND TIME<930;
OP_IN:=TIME>=930 AND TIME<1030;
OP_START:=OP_IN AND REF(OP_IN,1)=0;

{========== CONFIRMED SWING POINTS ==========}
{TWO CLOSED CANDLES ON EACH SIDE}

SW_H:=REF(H,3)>REF(H,4) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,5) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,2) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,1);

SW_L:=REF(L,3)<REF(L,4) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,5) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,2) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,1);

{========== PREMARKET SWINGS ==========}

PM_H_EVT:=SW_H AND REF(PM_IN,3);
PM_L_EVT:=SW_L AND REF(PM_IN,3);

{========== OPENING SESSION SWINGS ==========}

OP_H_EVT:=SW_H AND REF(OP_IN,3);
OP_L_EVT:=SW_L AND REF(OP_IN,3);

{========== PREMARKET PIVOT LABELS ==========}

DRAWTEXT(REFX(PM_H_EVT,3),H+12,'PMH'),COLORCYAN;

DRAWTEXT(REFX(PM_L_EVT,3),L-12,'PML'),COLORCYAN;

{========== OPENING PIVOT LABELS ==========}

DRAWTEXT(REFX(OP_H_EVT,3),H+12,'OH'),COLORLIGREEN;

DRAWTEXT(REFX(OP_L_EVT,3),L-12,'OL'),COLORLIRED;

{========== CONFIRMED BEFORE OPEN ==========}

PM_H_READY:=PM_H_EVT AND PM_IN;
PM_L_READY:=PM_L_EVT AND PM_IN;

{========== LAST PREMARKET LEVELS ==========}

PM_H_VALUE:=VALUEWHEN(PM_H_READY,REF(H,3));
PM_L_VALUE:=VALUEWHEN(PM_L_READY,REF(L,3));

PM_H_DATE:=VALUEWHEN(PM_H_READY,DATE);
PM_L_DATE:=VALUEWHEN(PM_L_READY,DATE);

{========== FREEZE LEVELS AT 9:30 ==========}

OPEN_PM_H:=VALUEWHEN(OP_START,PM_H_VALUE);
OPEN_PM_L:=VALUEWHEN(OP_START,PM_L_VALUE);

OPEN_H_DATE:=VALUEWHEN(OP_START,PM_H_DATE);
OPEN_L_DATE:=VALUEWHEN(OP_START,PM_L_DATE);

{========== DISPLAY OPENING LEVELS ==========}

PM_SWING_HIGH:IF(OP_IN AND OPEN_H_DATE=DATE,OPEN_PM_H,DRAWNULL),COLORCYAN;

PM_SWING_LOW:IF(OP_IN AND OPEN_L_DATE=DATE,OPEN_PM_L,DRAWNULL),COLORLIBLUE;

{========== LEVEL LABELS ==========}

DRAWTEXT(OP_START AND OPEN_H_DATE=DATE,OPEN_PM_H+12,'PM HIGH'),COLORCYAN;

DRAWTEXT(OP_START AND OPEN_L_DATE=DATE,OPEN_PM_L-12,'PM LOW'),COLORLIBLUE;


### What you'll see at 9:30 AM

The indicator takes the most recent **confirmed pre-market swing high and swing low** known at the opening bell and draws their levels throughout the first hour.

As the opening session develops, additional swing highs and lows appear with `OH` and `OL` labels. Those are separate from the pre-market reference levels.

This uses actual confirmed swing pivots, not necessarily the absolute pre-market highest and lowest prices.

### Important: Confirmation and repainting

The script compares a potential pivot against two candles before it and two fully closed candles afterward. It then places the label back on the original pivot using `REFX`.

Therefore, a label appears historically at the pivot, but **is only known after the two subsequent candles have closed**. A swing formed near the end of a session can be labeled after that session finishes; however, only swings confirmed before 9:30 AM are used for the frozen pre-market reference levels.

|---|---|

| Language | Mai Language |
| Exhibition Area | Main |
| Chart | 5m |

LH_SIG:=PH AND PREVH>0 AND CH<PREVH;

LL_SIG:=PL AND PREVL>0 AND CL<PREVL;

LOW_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PL,CL);

BOS_DN:=DN_BREAK AND OLD_DIR<>1;

CHOCH_DN:=DN_BREAK AND OLD_DIR=1;

DN_GAP:=MAX(L-LOW_LEVEL,0);

DN_VOL:=LOW_LEVEL+DN_GAP*REL_VOL;

## How the new volume display works

The volume histogram is calculated from each candle's volume compared with the previous 20-candle average.

- Normal volume fills approximately 50% of the available vertical gap between the structure line and the candle wick.
- Double the average volume fills approximately 100% of that gap.
- Smaller volume produces shorter bars.

The visualization is limited to the **12 most recent 5-minute candles before a confirmed BOS or CHoCH**, so it stays relatively compact.

Importantly, this is a relative-volume visualization, **not a true volume profile or bid/ask volume delta**. It uses candle volume and the available price-space geometry to determine each bar's size.

Because the display windows use `BACKSET`, their historical volume bars are drawn retrospectively after a structure break is confirmed. The existing `NOT(ISLASTBAR)` condition also means a live break won't be marked until it is no longer on the chart's last candle.

**Yes, but there's an important distinction with our current MNQMS V5 indicator.**

When you're watching MNQ candles develop in real time or using chart replay, the indicators should update as new candles become available. However, **some elements in our current code appear retrospectively rather than building gradually.**

Here's what happens:

| Indicator | When it appears |
|---|---|
| HH / LH / HL / LL | After two additional 5-minute candles confirm the swing |
| BOS | After price breaks a swing level and the break is confirmed |
| CHoCH | After an opposite-direction structure break is confirmed |
| Volume histogram | Currently drawn backward over previous candles once BOS or CHoCH is detected |

### The issue with V5

We use two functions that affect chart replay:

- `REFX`: Places confirmed swing labels back on the original pivot candle.
- `BACKSET`: Draws the volume histogram backward across candles preceding a structure break.

For example, imagine a BOS happens at 10:15 AM. The current volume visualization may suddenly appear over multiple earlier candles at once, rather than growing candle by candle.

### What I recommend for V6

I would make **MNQMS replay-friendly and non-backpainting**.

That means:

1. Swing points are detected and confirmed as candles close.
2. BOS and CHoCH appear only when their conditions are confirmed.
3. Volume bars develop progressively as each candle forms or closes.
4. The dotted structure lines stay attached to their respective levels.
5. Historical data won't reveal signals before they could have been known.

One tradeoff: we can place a swing label on its original candle *after confirmation*, but it will appear there retrospectively. For strictly chronological replay, we'd instead place the signal on its confirmation candle.

**My recommendation:** Build V6 so you can watch the MNQ 5-minute chart in replay and see the market structure develop naturally, without future information leaking into earlier candles.

That's especially useful if you're using replay to practice identifying entries based on BOS and CHoCH.

### ASSISTANT 2026-10-17 07:59
The moomoo Backtest tool can actually be very useful for your MNQ trading, especially because you've been building indicators around **price action, market structure, BOS, CHoCH, and the London/New York sessions**.

But there's one important concept to understand:

**Backtesting tells you how a strategy performed in the past. It does not tell you whether the next trade will win.**

And you don't need to use a moving-average strategy. We can design a backtest around your own price-action rules.

## 1. What the Backtest tool actually does

Imagine you tell moomoo:

> Every time the 5-minute moving average crosses above the 20-minute moving average, buy. Sell when it crosses below.

Moomoo takes historical market data and simulates what would have happened if you had followed those rules.

It can then calculate metrics such as:

| Metric | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| Total return | How much the simulated strategy made or lost |
| Win rate | Percentage of trades that were profitable |
| Maximum drawdown | Largest peak-to-trough decline in the backtest |
| Number of trades | How many entries the strategy generated |
| Profit factor | Gross profits divided by gross losses |
| Equity curve | How the simulated account balance changed |

The exact metrics available depend on the type of backtest you're using.

### What does April 16, 2026 mean?

If April 16 is shown as the start of your backtest period, it means the simulation begins evaluating trades from that date, using the historical data available.

It doesn't mean moomoo is predicting the market from April 16 onward.

For example, a backtest covering April 16 to October 16, 2026 would examine six months of historical trading activity.

**A positive return means those rules were profitable in that historical simulation, not that they'll necessarily be profitable tomorrow.**

## 3. Why you're not seeing B and S on your chart

There are two different things in moomoo:

**A. MNQMS indicator signals**

Your indicator calculates `BUY_SIGNAL` and `SELL_SIGNAL`. These produce numerical values that the backtester can read, but they don't automatically draw B and S letters.

**B. Backtest executions**

When you run the backtest, moomoo can simulate orders based on those signals. In your earlier moving-average backtest, the B and S markers appeared because the simulation had generated trades.

So here's what to check after pressing **Backtest**:

1. Wait for the backtest to finish.
2. Check the backtest candlestick chart for B/S markers.
3. Open **History** and check whether there are filled orders.
4. Check **Log** for rejected or unfilled orders if no trades appear.

If there are no simulated trades, the problem may be the signal calculation, available futures data, or order-sizing configuration—not the chart display.

Moomoo also has a separate *Trade Marking* feature for actual executed orders. Those markers should not be confused with simulated backtest trades. <Cite ref="turn555850search9"/>

### If you want B and S on your regular MNQ chart

Add these two lines to the end of your MNQMS indicator:


{========== BUY AND SELL LABELS ==========}

DRAWTEXT(BUY_SIGNAL>0,L-30,'B'),COLORLIGREEN;

DRAWTEXT(SELL_SIGNAL>0,H+30,'S'),COLORLIRED;


These would mark **signals**, not actual order executions. In the existing code, signals may not appear on the currently forming candle because of `NOT(ISLASTBAR)`.

Run the complete April 16–October 16 baseline first. Then split the data so that you aren't judging the strategy only on the period used to develop it.

|---|---|---|

| Out-of-sample | Oct 1 – Oct 16, 2026 | Test the frozen rules on unseen dates |

The second period is short, so treat it as an initial check rather than definitive proof.

I would pay particular attention to **maximum drawdown in dollars**, maximum consecutive losses, net profit after commissions, and whether the strategy trades outside your intended New York session. The current MNQMS backtest does not automatically enforce your proposed stop-loss, take-profit, or daily loss limits.

| Runner | Keep 1 long | Keep 1 short |
| Trailing stop | Move upward | Move downward |

## How I would translate this into a backtest

Your discretionary decisions can't all be reproduced perfectly by an automated strategy. But we can create a systematic approximation and compare it against your actual trading.

I would divide the logic into three parts.

**1. Structure-based initial stop**

For a short trade, place the stop above the relevant confirmed swing high, with a small buffer. For a long, place it below the relevant swing low.

Use 10 points as the initial reference, but calculate the actual risk from the structure level *before entering*. If the required stop is too wide for your risk budget, skip the trade or reduce size rather than increase the risk after entry.

**2. Flexible TP1**

Start with a 1R target, typically around 10 points, but check whether an opposing swing level creates an obstacle before that target. We can test a version that takes TP1 at the nearer of 1R or a predefined structural target.

Once TP1 fills, the remaining contract's stop moves to the entry price, accounting for slippage and execution limitations.

**3. Trailing TP2**

We can automate the objective parts:

- For longs, trail below newly confirmed higher lows.
- For shorts, trail above newly confirmed lower highs.
- Never loosen an existing trailing stop.
- Exit on a confirmed opposing structure signal, trailing stop, or intraday cutoff.

Your discretionary decision to take profits when momentum weakens can become an additional test rule—for example, an opposing CHoCH or a failed continuation after a retest.

  | Forced flat | 11:55 AM ET for initial test |


These are **test assumptions**, not claims about an optimal or profitable strategy. The relatively early forced-flat time deliberately isolates your morning scalp performance.

## 2. Exact entry conditions

I recommend starting with a **confirmed BOS-close entry**, rather than a discretionary retest entry. It is easier to define precisely and avoids ambiguous fills.

**Long entry:**

1. A confirmed swing high exists, detected using two candles on either side.
2. A completed 5-minute candle closes strictly above that swing high.
3. This is the first valid break of that swing level.
4. The candle is confirmed during your entry window.
5. There is no existing position, no pending entry, and daily risk limits permit another trade.
6. Buy 2 MNQ at the next bar's executable opening price.

**Short entry:** Reverse these conditions. A completed candle must close below the most recent confirmed swing low.

For V1, treat both BOS and CHoCH as qualifying break events. Record their classifications separately so we can compare them later.

Only closed-candle information may generate an entry. The signals must not rely on the retrospectively drawn `REFX` or `BACKSET` graphics in your visual MNQMS indicator.

## 3. Structural stop-loss and TP1

For a long, use the latest confirmed swing low preceding entry; for a short, use the latest confirmed swing high.


  Initial stop placement
  \[
  \begin{aligned}
  SL_{\text{long}} &= \text{Swing Low}-2\\
  SL_{\text{short}} &= \text{Swing High}+2
  \end{aligned}
  \]

  After filling the entry, calculate \(R\), the number of points between entry and stop.

  Accept the trade only when the stop distance is between **5 and 15 points**. If the structural stop requires more than 15 points, skip the trade instead of artificially tightening it.


TP1 closes one contract at 1R. After the TP1 execution is confirmed, replace the remaining contract's stop with a breakeven stop at the actual entry price.

The BE adjustment must happen as soon as TP1 fills, not at the next 5-minute candle close in a live-capable implementation.

## 4. How to trail the runner

I would use this specific structure-based rule:

- **Long:** Trail below each newly confirmed higher swing low minus 2 points.
- **Short:** Trail above each newly confirmed lower swing high plus 2 points.
- Adjust the stop only in the profitable direction.
- Never lower a long stop or raise a short stop once it has been tightened.
- Exit the runner if its stop triggers, a confirmed opposite BOS/CHoCH occurs, or the 11:55 AM cutoff arrives.

An opposite signal is an exit condition, not automatic permission to reverse the position.

For a robust backtest, evaluate protective stops and targets against intrabar prices, not only candle closes.

The key question is not simply which setting generates the most profit. We want to identify which stop ceiling offers the best balance of:

- Net expectancy after fees and slippage.
- Number of qualifying trades.
- Maximum drawdown and worst losing streak.
- Frequency of stop-outs before price reaches TP1.
- Runner contribution to total net profit.

If the 15-point version has better expectancy than the 10-point version but makes too few trades, that's important. If the 20-point version only works because of a few unusually large winners, that's also important.

## 6. Backtest sequence I recommend


  
    
      **Test 1 — Structural stop sensitivity**

      Compare 8, 10, 12, 15, and 20-point maximum stops. Keep TP1 at 1R, runner trailing fixed, and trading hours unchanged.
    
    
      **Test 2 — TP1 sensitivity**

      Compare 0.75R, 1R, 1.25R, and 1.5R. This will help determine whether taking profits earlier is actually beneficial after transaction costs.
    
    
      **Test 3 — Runner management**

      Compare swing trailing, a fixed 10-point trail after BE, and exiting the runner upon an opposing structure break.
    
    
      **Test 4 — Entry quality**

      Compare immediate BOS entries, immediate CHoCH entries, and entries after a confirmed retest.
    
    
      **Test 5 — Trading window**

      Compare 9:35–10:30, 9:35–11:30, and 10:00–11:30 AM ET.
    
  


For your August 1–October 16 historical dataset, I'd initially use August–September for development and October 1–16 as an untouched validation period. Since that holdout is short, ideally we'd obtain additional historical data for a stronger out-of-sample test.

## 7. Important implementation requirements

Before coding the execution engine, these details should be fixed:

**First:** The strategy needs to track an entire two-contract trade as one setup with two legs. Otherwise, the backtester might interpret TP1 as a new short entry rather than closing one long contract.

**Second:** The initial protective stop must remain active until TP1 fills. After partial profit-taking, the remaining stop quantity must be updated safely. TP1 and the protective stop should be coordinated so they cannot accidentally over-close the position.

**Third:** If TP1 and the initial stop are both touched inside the same five-minute candle, the engine must not automatically assume that TP1 happened first. Use lower-timeframe or tick data when available; otherwise, report ambiguous fills separately or use the conservative stop-first assumption.

**Fourth:** The strategy must mark to market every open position when measuring daily and maximum drawdown. A $50K prop-firm account's allowable loss is not necessarily 4% or 5% of the headline balance; the exact rule must match your firm's evaluation.

**Fifth:** The visual MNQMS indicator stays untouched. The new backtesting engine should use only information that was knowable at the time of each trade.

There is one tooling limitation: **I haven't verified that moomoo's Indicator Backtest can express partial exits, dynamic stop replacements, or runner-specific state management.** Its simpler buy/sell condition screen may not be sufficient. The implementation may require its Custom Algo Strategy functionality, or a separate backtest engine if that functionality cannot simulate the full order lifecycle.

## My recommended first build

**MNQMS Scalper V1:** Two contracts, 9:35–11:30 entries, confirmed BOS/CHoCH, structural stop with a 15-point ceiling, TP1 at 1R, runner to BE immediately after TP1, confirmed-swing trailing, and forced flat at 11:55 AM.

Then test **maximum structural stop distance first**, because it determines which setups you can take, the risk per entry, and whether your usual 10-point starting stop is practical.

This gives us a systematic baseline that reflects your actual scalping style before attempting to automate the more discretionary decisions you make while watching the candles.

| Overnight holdings | Never intentionally held |

**Critical:** Ten points is a reference, not a rigid stop or target. The trader places stops beyond meaningful swing levels so ordinary retests do not prematurely stop out a trade.

The trader actively adjusts TP2 and may exit before the trailing stop triggers.

### Example: 2-contract short scalp

Entry at 30,000, initial stop at 30,010, TP1 at 29,990.

- Initial risk: 10 points × $2 × 2 contracts = **$40** before costs.
- TP1: Cover 1 contract at 29,990, banking **$20** before costs.
- Move the remaining contract's stop to 30,000.
- Trail the runner downward behind confirmed lower highs.
- Close on trailing stop, opposing structural signal, discretionary weakness, or intraday cutoff.

The second contract provides the possibility of making more than the initial 1R scalp.

## 3. Chart Indicator B — MNQMS Market Structure

This is the main technical-analysis indicator.

### Capabilities developed

- Higher High (HH)
- Higher Low (HL)
- Lower High (LH)
- Lower Low (LL)
- Bullish and bearish Break of Structure (BOS)
- Bullish and bearish Change of Character (CHoCH)
- Dotted horizontal structure lines
- Colored structure labels
- Volume-based visual bars near broken structure levels
- Buy and Sell signal outputs for backtesting
- Optional live-chart B and S text labels

### Version history

| Version | Main changes | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | Confirmed pivot detection and HH/LH/HL/LL | Initially blank |
| V2 | Simplified swing detection using `HHV`, `LLV`, `VALUEWHEN` | Swing labels subsequently appeared |
| V3 | Added BOS detection and horizontal structure lines | BOS visible, but visual clutter |
| V4 | Added CHoCH and separate BOS/CHoCH colors | Proposed; full compilation not independently verified |
| V5 | Dotted lines plus relative-volume bars | Latest enhanced design |
| V5 color update | Muted volume-bar colors to simulate translucency | Proposed visual modification |

### Structure classification

A swing is based on a five-candle pattern: two candles to the left, the pivot candle, and two candles to the right.

Higher and lower classifications compare each confirmed swing against the preceding swing of the same type.

BOS/CHoCH logic in V4/V5 uses the direction of the previous structure break:

- Bullish break after bullish direction → BOS
- Bearish break after bearish direction → BOS
- Bullish break after bearish direction → CHoCH
- Bearish break after bullish direction → CHoCH

This is a **simplified classification**, not a complete protected-high/protected-low smart-money-concepts engine.

### Final visual configuration

| Event | Structure line | Label |
|---|---|---|
| HH / LH / HL / LL | None | White |
| Bullish BOS | Green dotted | Green BOS |
| Bearish BOS | Red dotted | Red BOS |
| Bullish CHoCH | Cyan dotted | Cyan CHoCH |
| Bearish CHoCH | Orange dotted | Orange CHoCH |

Relative-volume bars were designed to extend from the dotted structure line toward price candles.

The proposed volume normalization is:


AVG_VOL:=MAX(MA(VOL,20),1);
REL_VOL:=MIN(VOL/AVG_VOL,2)/2;


Volume visualizations were limited to approximately 12 candles before a detected break using `BACKSET`.

The preferred muted colors were:


COLOR1B684F
COLOR7F3B42
COLOR147E89
COLOR7F522D


True alpha transparency for `STICKLINE` was not verified; these are muted solid colors.

### Known implementation limitations

**Very important for backtesting:** V5 uses `REFX` and `BACKSET` to draw historical information retrospectively.

The visual indicator must not be treated as proof that every displayed historical mark was available at that time.

A separate backtest strategy must generate signals from already-confirmed candle data and avoid historical look-ahead or backpainting.

Also, the current code uses `NOT(ISLASTBAR)` in places to suppress unfinished-bar signals. This may delay when marks appear in live use.

### Proposed initial parameters

| Setting | V1 specification |

| Starting account | $50,000 USD |

These are **proposed test parameters**, not necessarily the trader's exact discretionary behavior or platform settings already implemented.

### Long entry specification

A long entry requires:

1. A previously confirmed swing high exists.
2. A completed 5-minute candle closes strictly above that swing high.
3. This is the first break of that structure level.
4. The signal occurs within the allowed trading window.
5. No current position or pending entry exists.
6. The structural stop distance is acceptable.
7. The daily loss guard and trade-count limit allow entry.

Short entry is symmetrical, with a close beneath a confirmed swing low.

Both BOS and CHoCH are eligible in V1. Record their categories separately for analysis.

### Stop-loss specification

Long stop:

\[
SL_{\text{long}}=\text{Confirmed Swing Low}-2
\]

Short stop:

\[
SL_{\text{short}}=\text{Confirmed Swing High}+2
\]

Entry-to-stop distance must initially be between 5 and 15 points.

Skip setups requiring wider stops rather than arbitrarily tightening them.

### TP1 and BE

- Submit two contracts with appropriate protective exits.
- TP1 is 1R from actual entry, closing one contract.
- Immediately upon confirmed TP1 fill, move the remaining contract's stop to the entry price.
- Properly reduce outstanding stop quantity after TP1.
- Do not accidentally reverse the position or over-close through conflicting orders.

BE means gross breakeven, not guaranteed net breakeven after commissions and slippage.

### Runner management

For longs, trail below newly confirmed higher swing lows with a 2-point buffer.

For shorts, trail above newly confirmed lower swing highs with a 2-point buffer.

Never loosen the stop.

Exit the runner on:

- Trailing stop execution.
- Confirmed opposing structural signal.
- Forced intraday flattening.

The trader's discretionary decision to exit on fading momentum is not fully captured yet.

## 9. Open technical questions and limitations

These must be resolved before treating the new backtest as valid.

**A. Platform capability:** Can moomoo Indicator Backtest simulate two separately managed exit legs, bracket-order quantity changes, stop-to-BE adjustment, and a structural trailing stop? We have not verified this. Moomoo Custom Algo Strategy may be necessary, or an external backtesting engine.

**B. Historical execution:** If a stop and TP1 are touched within the same five-minute bar, the test cannot simply assume the profitable order filled first. Prefer tick or one-minute data; otherwise use conservative assumptions.

**C. Contract rollover:** The earlier continuous-contract backtest showed trades on different quarterly futures contracts. The new engine needs explicit rollover logic and should not introduce artificial P&L jumps.

**D. Session times:** Confirm whether moomoo uses exchange time, Eastern Time, or another timezone, particularly for the London session and daylight-saving transitions.

**E. Prop-firm rules:** The exact firm is not yet identified. Maximum trailing drawdown, unrealized P&L treatment, daily loss rules, and required flattening times must come from the selected firm's current rulebook.

**F. Entry classification:** The existing simplified BOS/CHoCH logic may differ from the trader's discretionary structure interpretation. Keep both signal types recorded separately.

**G. Runner judgment:** The trader often adjusts TP2 and exits when momentum fades. A mechanical structural stop is only an approximation; this remains an important area for improvement.

**H. Backtest signal timing:** Historical drawing commands may repaint/backpaint. Trade entry signals must be produced from confirmed information available at that bar, not from shifted visual annotations.

**I. Open-position risk:** The daily $250 loss guard should consider unrealized adverse P&L, and the backtest should mark open positions to market continuously.

**J. Entry signal frequency:** The first strategy only produced three orders. Confirm the new backtester generates sufficient qualifying setups and that no output-registration or order-state issue suppresses trades.

**Build the signal engine first, then verify the backtest engine, then implement trade management.**

I checked moomoo's documentation. Its Custom Algo Strategy builder supports conditional branches, position checks, order placement, and separate take-profit/stop-loss logic. However, I could not verify that the simpler **Indicator Backtest** supports two independent exit legs, immediate breakeven adjustment, and swing-based trailing. <Cite refs={["turn266805search0","turn266805search4"]}/>

So we should use two separate development stages:

For the trailing rule, use:

\[
SL_{\text{long,new}}=\max(SL_{\text{old}}, BE, HL-2)
\]

\[

\]

Here, HL/LH means the most recent **confirmed** structural swing suitable for protecting the trade. The runner stop must never move against the position.

The most critical implementation detail is the TP1 fill transition. **Only move the runner to BE after the first contract actually closes**, not merely because the candle touches TP1.

## 2. Paste-ready Mai Language code — `MNQSCALP_SIG`

This is the first implementation to compile and validate. It uses the functions from the supplied Mai Language list and does not use `BACKSET` or future-looking `REFX`.

Moomoo's official indicator documentation confirms its custom indicator editor and named formula outputs. It also notes that not all formula functions are available in every context, so compilation and historical signal verification remain necessary. <Cite ref="turn415425search0"/>


{MNQSCALP SIGNAL ENGINE V1}
{MNQ 5 MINUTE CHART}
{CONFIRMED BOS CHOCH BREAKOUTS}
{NO BACKSET OR REFX}

{========== SETTINGS ==========}

BUFFER:=2;
MINSTOP:=5;
MAXSTOP:=15;

{========== CONFIRMED PIVOTS ==========}
{ALL REFERENCED CANDLES ARE CLOSED}

PH:=REF(H,3)>REF(H,4) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,5) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,2) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,1);

PL:=REF(L,3)<REF(L,4) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,5) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,2) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,1);

{========== CONFIRMED LEVELS ==========}

HLEV:=VALUEWHEN(PH,REF(H,3));
LLEV:=VALUEWHEN(PL,REF(L,3));

{========== CLOSED BAR BREAKOUT ==========}

UP_CROSS:=REF(HLEV,1)>0 AND REF(C,1)>REF(HLEV,1) AND REF(C,2)<=REF(HLEV,2);

DN_CROSS:=REF(LLEV,1)>0 AND REF(C,1)<REF(LLEV,1) AND REF(C,2)>=REF(LLEV,2);

{========== FIRST BREAK ONLY ==========}

UP_FIRST:=UP_CROSS AND COUNT(UP_CROSS,BARSLAST(PH)+1)=1;

DN_FIRST:=DN_CROSS AND COUNT(DN_CROSS,BARSLAST(PL)+1)=1;

{========== NEW YORK ENTRY WINDOW ==========}

SESSION_OK:=TIME>=940 AND TIME<1130;

{========== STRUCTURAL STOP LEVELS ==========}

LONG_STOP:=REF(LLEV,1)-BUFFER;
SHORT_STOP:=REF(HLEV,1)+BUFFER;

{========== RISK AT CURRENT BAR OPEN ==========}

LONG_RISK:=O-LONG_STOP;
SHORT_RISK:=SHORT_STOP-O;

LONG_RISK_OK:=REF(LLEV,1)>0 AND LONG_RISK>=MINSTOP AND LONG_RISK<=MAXSTOP;

SHORT_RISK_OK:=REF(HLEV,1)>0 AND SHORT_RISK>=MINSTOP AND SHORT_RISK<=MAXSTOP;

{========== RAW BREAK SIGNALS ==========}

RAW_LONG:IF(UP_FIRST AND SESSION_OK,1,0),NODRAW;

RAW_SHORT:IF(DN_FIRST AND SESSION_OK,1,0),NODRAW;

{========== FILTERED ENTRY SIGNALS ==========}

LONG_ENTRY:IF(UP_FIRST AND SESSION_OK AND LONG_RISK_OK,1,0),NODRAW;

SHORT_ENTRY:IF(DN_FIRST AND SESSION_OK AND SHORT_RISK_OK,1,0),NODRAW;

{========== TIME BASED EXIT ==========}

FLAT_TIME:=TIME>=1155 AND TIME<1700 AND REF(TIME,1)<1155;

{========== EXIT SIGNALS ==========}

EXIT_LONG:IF(DN_FIRST OR FLAT_TIME,1,0),NODRAW;

EXIT_SHORT:IF(UP_FIRST OR FLAT_TIME,1,0),NODRAW;

{========== BACKTEST COMPATIBILITY ==========}

BUY_SIGNAL:IF(UP_FIRST AND SESSION_OK AND LONG_RISK_OK,1,0),NODRAW;

SELL_SIGNAL:IF(DN_FIRST OR FLAT_TIME,1,0),NODRAW;

ZERO_SIGNAL:0,NODRAW;


### Important implementation details

This indicator deliberately separates **raw entry signals** from **risk-filtered entry signals**. If no trades appear, we can determine whether the problem is the breakout logic, time window, or stop-distance filter.

`LONG_ENTRY` and `SHORT_ENTRY` signal on the bar following a completed breakout candle. They use that bar's opening price as a proposed entry-price estimate.

However, **this code does not itself place orders, track positions, count trades, or manage stops**.

`SELL_SIGNAL` is mapped to `EXIT_LONG`, not to `SHORT_ENTRY`, because the previous simple backtest behaved like a long-entry/long-exit system. We must test short positions separately unless the platform explicitly supports them.

The forced-flat output is a signal at the cutoff, not a guaranteed executed liquidation. The backtester must be checked for whether it executes orders on the signal bar or the following bar.

The code also deliberately excludes a higher-timeframe trend filter, volume confirmation, retest requirement, and daily trade limit. Those are separate experiments.

# MNQSCALP — Bidirectional Strategy & Optimization Plan

**Decision: MNQSCALP must support both long and short trades, with trend alignment as a separate filter.** A bullish BOS does not automatically mean the overall trend is bullish, and a bearish BOS does not automatically mean the overall trend is bearish.

For V1, I recommend testing trend continuation separately from CHoCH reversals. This will help us identify whether the trader performs better following established trends, trading reversals, or both.

## 1. Does the current MNQSCALP_SIG handle both directions?

**Partially.** It calculates `LONG_ENTRY` and `SHORT_ENTRY`, but it does not yet properly enforce trend alignment or manage independent long and short positions.

There are also two code-level issues to correct before testing.

### Issue A — Structure breaks aren't equivalent to trend direction

The current system detects:

- A close above a confirmed swing high → bullish break.
- A close below a confirmed swing low → bearish break.

But price can break a minor swing high during a strong downtrend. That would generate a bullish signal even though the larger structure remains bearish.

We should separate:

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Market structure | Identify confirmed HH, HL, LH, LL |
| Trend state | Decide bullish, bearish, or neutral |
| BOS | Identify a break consistent with trend |
| CHoCH | Identify a potential change against trend |
| Trade filter | Permit or reject a setup based on the strategy being tested |

### Issue B — The current signal code needs correction

The current `UP_CROSS` and `DN_CROSS` logic compares previous closes against historical levels, and the resulting signals are evaluated on the next candle.

That can be appropriate for next-bar execution, but **the current first-break detection is not robust**: `COUNT(UP_CROSS,BARSLAST(PH)+1)` can count break events across an interval whose boundaries don't align with the referenced historical level.

Additionally, the current code doesn't track the open position, and `SELL_SIGNAL` is specifically mapped to exiting longs.

We should revise the signal engine before interpreting its backtest returns.

## Recommended trend filter

Use a strict swing-structure definition as the baseline:

**Bullish trend:** The two most recent confirmed swing highs and lows establish HH + HL.

**Bearish trend:** The two most recent confirmed swing highs and lows establish LH + LL.

**Neutral:** Any mixed or incomplete structure.

Only allow:

- Long entries on confirmed bullish breaks in bullish trends.
- Short entries on confirmed bearish breaks in bearish trends.
- No continuation entries in neutral structure.

CHoCH signals should be recorded separately as reversal candidates, not automatically traded against the established trend.

This is a more relevant baseline than introducing a moving average immediately, because the trader's actual approach is price-action-based.

## 2. Optimization sequence — prioritize robust win rate

The goal is to improve the percentage of trades that win **without sacrificing overall profitability or breaching the prop-account loss limit**.

A system with an 80% win rate can still lose money if the losing trades are disproportionately large. Therefore, optimize using win rate alongside net expectancy, profit factor, drawdown, and trade frequency.

### Recommended optimization order

| Order | Parameter | Values to test | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Signal correctness | Fixed | Eliminate look-ahead, duplicate breaks and timing errors before optimizing |
| 1 | Trend filter | None; HH+HL/LH+LL; EMA 20/50 alignment | Establish whether trading with trend improves setup quality |
| 2 | Entry type | BOS only; CHoCH only; both | Separate continuation and reversal performance |
| 3 | Trading session | 9:35–10:30; 9:35–11:30; 10:00–11:30 ET | Identify the strongest time window |
| 4 | Swing sensitivity | 2+2; 3+3; 4+4 candles | Control how much minor market noise creates signals |
| 5 | Maximum stop distance | 8, 10, 12, 15, 20 points | Find a practical structural risk ceiling |
| 6 | Structural buffer | 1, 2, 3, 5 points | Determine how much room stops need for normal retests |
| 7 | TP1 | 0.75R, 1R, 1.25R, 1.5R | Optimize first-contract exit after the entry system is fixed |
| 8 | Runner management | Confirmed swing; fixed 10-point trail; opposing signal | Evaluate the contribution of the second contract |

**Hold `MINSTOP=5` initially.** Once the other key parameters are stable, test minimum distances of 3, 5, 8, and 10 points.

Why trend filter first rather than stop distance? Because the initial question is whether we're taking good trades in the correct direction. Changing stop distance before distinguishing continuation setups from countertrend breaks can hide that problem.

### How to run the tests efficiently

Start with three signal groups: raw bullish/bearish breaks, trend-aligned BOS, and countertrend CHoCH. Evaluate each group separately with identical execution assumptions.

After identifying a viable entry family, compare session windows and swing sensitivity. Then optimize structural stops and trade management using the full two-contract engine.

Do not select a winner based purely on the highest in-sample win rate. Treat August–September 2026 as development data and October 1–16 as a preliminary untouched test. That holdout is short; extend the history before trusting the result.

For each configuration, export the number of setups, completed trades, win rate, average winner, average loser, net expectancy after costs, profit factor, maximum drawdown, and TP1/runner contributions.

LVALID:=COUNT(PL,0)>=2;

SHORT_SL:=REF(HLEV,1)+BUFFER;

SHORT_RISK:=SHORT_SL-O;

## 2. Trend filter logic

The strict baseline is:

| Market structure | Trend | Trading permission |
|---|---|---|
| HH + HL | Bullish | Long continuation entries |
| LH + LL | Bearish | Short continuation entries |
| Mixed structure | Neutral | No continuation entries |
| Bullish break during downtrend | Potential CHoCH | Record, don't trade in V2 |
| Bearish break during uptrend | Potential CHoCH | Record, don't trade in V2 |

This deliberately prioritizes trend-aligned BOS entries. CHoCH entries are available as separate classifications for later comparison.

**First-break logic:** The script counts closes beyond the most recently confirmed swing level since its confirmation. Only the first qualifying close produces a breakout signal; a later recross of the same level should not trigger again.

The signal is produced on the candle after the breakout has closed, using that candle's opening price for the initial stop-distance calculation.

One limitation: a newly confirmed swing replaces the tracked level even if a previous one has not broken. That is intentional for this baseline.

| MNQZ26 | Yes |
| MNQ continuous | Yes |
| Other MNQ expiries | Yes |

## 3. Should we switch to ATR stops?

**Yes, test ATR-based stops, but retain structural stops as the benchmark.**

The 39–239-point structural stop distances suggest that the most recent opposite swing is often too far away for the trader's intended short-duration scalp.

This doesn't necessarily mean that 100-point stops are good. It may mean we're using the wrong scale of market structure to place the stop.

Compare three approaches:

| Stop model | Calculation |
|---|---|
| Structural | Opposite confirmed swing ± 2-point buffer |
| ATR | Entry ± \(k \times ATR(14)\) |
| Hybrid | Structural stop, accepting only trades where structural risk is within a multiple of ATR |

For the ATR model, start with multipliers of **0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, and 1.5**.

For example, if ATR(14) on the 5-minute chart is 40 points, a 0.5 ATR stop is 20 points and a 1.0 ATR stop is 40 points.

The important difference is that the ATR stop adapts to market volatility, whereas a fixed 10-point stop may be too narrow during volatile periods.

However, ATR is not a structural price level. An ATR stop can still be placed directly inside ordinary market noise or in front of an obvious retest.

The first-break rule prevents repeated entries around a level that price keeps crossing. Removing it prematurely could create many low-quality whipsaw trades.

Later, introduce a separately defined **break–retest–continuation** setup rather than simply permitting every recross.

### Exact rules for the first two new filters

**C3 — Candle-body confirmation**

Require the breakout candle to close beyond the structure level by at least 20% of its own full high-low range.

For bullish breaks:

\[
\frac{Close-Level}{High-Low} \geq 0.20
\]

For bearish breaks:

\[
\frac{Level-Close}{High-Low} \geq 0.20
\]

Exclude zero-range candles.

Test thresholds of `0.10`, `0.20`, and `0.30`, but start with `0.20`.

**C4 — Volume confirmation**

Require:

\[
Volume_{\text{break}} \geq 1.2\times SMA(Volume,20)
\]

Use only data available at the confirmed breakout candle close.

Test `1.0×`, `1.2×`, and `1.5×` after verifying the baseline.

**C5 — Retest confirmation**

After a valid breakout, allow up to three additional 5-minute candles for a retest of the broken level.

For longs, price must touch the level and subsequently close above it. Shorts are symmetrical.

Enter no earlier than the next executable candle, and cancel the setup if price closes back through the level before confirmation.

This needs a state-aware implementation, not simply a historical `BACKSET` marker.

## 3. M2 — TP1 at 1R, BE, then fixed 10-point trailing stop

### State transitions

### Exact 10-point trailing formula

For a **long runner**:

\[
SL_t=\max(Entry,\ SL_{t-1},\ HighestSinceTP1-10)
\]

For a **short runner**:

\[
SL_t=\min(Entry,\ SL_{t-1},\ LowestSinceTP1+10)
\]

The `HighestSinceTP1` / `LowestSinceTP1` variable starts at the **TP1 execution price**, not the original entry price.

#### Example — Long

Entry at 30,000, \(R=20\) points, TP1 at 30,020.

| Event | Runner stop |
|---|---:|
| Initial entry | 29,980 |
| TP1 fills at 30,020 | 30,000 (BE) |
| Price reaches 30,025 | 30,015 |
| Price reaches 30,035 | 30,025 |
| Price falls to 30,025 | Runner exits at 30,025 |

The runner earns 25 points, while TP1 earns 20 points.

**Important:** Updating the trail from a candle's high and then checking that same candle's low can introduce an impossible execution sequence. Use intrabar sequencing, or conservatively activate bar-derived trail updates on the next bar.

For historical 5-minute OHLC testing, use this deterministic approximation:

1. At each bar opening, activate the runner stop carried over from the previous bar.
2. If the bar touches that stop, exit.
3. Otherwise, update the favorable extreme using the completed bar.
4. Calculate the new trailing stop for the next bar.

For the bar in which TP1 first fills, apply BE immediately but do not assume a same-bar high was achieved after TP1 unless lower-timeframe data confirms it.

### Exact swing confirmation

Use the same 2-left/2-right swing method as the original MNQMS system.

A swing low at candle index \(i\) is confirmed only when candles \(i+1\) and \(i+2\) have completed.

A strict swing low requires:

\[
Low_i < Low_{i-2},Low_{i-1},Low_{i+1},Low_{i+2}
\]

A strict swing high requires the opposite inequality.

**Only swings confirmed after TP1 can initiate a new M3 trail adjustment.** Do not use historical pivot labels drawn backward onto the chart.

### Exact M3 trailing formulas

For a long:

\[
SL_t=\max(SL_{t-1},Entry,ConfirmedSwingLow-2)
\]

For a short:

\[
SL_t=\min(SL_{t-1},Entry,ConfirmedSwingHigh+2)
\]

Apply these candidate levels only if they actually tighten the existing stop.

A newly confirmed swing that would loosen the stop is ignored.

#### Example — Long

Entry 30,000; initial stop 29,980; TP1 30,020.

| Event | Runner stop |
|---|---:|
| Entry | 29,980 |
| TP1 fills | 30,000 |
| Confirmed swing low = 30,012 | 30,010 |
| Confirmed swing low = 30,027 | 30,025 |
| New swing low = 30,020 | Remains 30,025 |
| Price touches 30,025 | Runner exits |

If no qualifying swing confirms before 11:55, the runner stays at BE until stopped or forcibly closed.

### Swing-trail timing

If a swing at candle \(i\) becomes confirmed when candle \(i+2\) closes, its stop adjustment takes effect **no earlier than the next executable price after that close**.

For 5-minute OHLC data, use the following bar's open. Do not update the stop retroactively on candle \(i\).

| TP1 and new BE both touched in same bar | Without intrabar ordering, do not assume BE filled after TP1 |
| Runner's existing stop touched | Exit before calculating any new candle-close trailing adjustment |
| Price gaps favorably beyond TP1 | Fill at the first executable price according to your order model |
| Opposite signal occurs | For M1–M3 baseline, record it but do not exit; keep this comparison focused on stops/targets |
| Cutoff reached | Exit remaining position using the first executable cutoff price |

## Step 1 — Create MNQ SCALP V1

This first version will:

- Detect confirmed swing highs and lows (2 candles left, 2 right).
- Identify bullish and bearish breaks of market structure.
- Classify BOS and CHoCH using the direction of the previous break.
- Generate numerical Buy and Sell signals for moomoo's Indicator Backtest.
- Keep your original MNQ MS indicator unchanged.

### Paste this code into your new indicator


{MNQ SCALP V1}
{MARKET STRUCTURE SIGNALS}
{5 MINUTE CHART}

{===== SWING DETECTION =====}

PH:=REF(H,2)=HHV(H,5) AND REF(H,2)>REF(H,3) AND REF(H,2)>REF(H,1);

PL:=REF(L,2)=LLV(L,5) AND REF(L,2)<REF(L,3) AND REF(L,2)<REF(L,1);

CH:=REF(H,2);
CL:=REF(L,2);

{===== STRUCTURE LEVELS =====}

HIGH_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PH,CH);
LOW_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PL,CL);

{===== STRUCTURE BREAKS =====}

UP_BREAK:=HIGH_LEVEL>0 AND C>HIGH_LEVEL AND COUNT(C>HIGH_LEVEL,BARSLAST(PH)+1)=1;

DN_BREAK:=LOW_LEVEL>0 AND C<LOW_LEVEL AND COUNT(C<LOW_LEVEL,BARSLAST(PL)+1)=1;

{===== BREAK DIRECTION =====}

OLD_DIR:=REF(VALUEWHEN(UP_BREAK OR DN_BREAK,IF(UP_BREAK,1,-1)),1);

{===== BOS SIGNALS =====}

BOS_UP:=UP_BREAK AND OLD_DIR<>-1;
BOS_DN:=DN_BREAK AND OLD_DIR<>1;

{===== CHOCH SIGNALS =====}

CHOCH_UP:=UP_BREAK AND OLD_DIR=-1;
CHOCH_DN:=DN_BREAK AND OLD_DIR=1;

{===== BUY / SELL SIGNALS =====}

BUY_SIGNAL:IF(BOS_UP OR CHOCH_UP,1,0),NODRAW;

SELL_SIGNAL:IF(BOS_DN OR CHOCH_DN,1,0),NODRAW;

{===== VISUAL SIGNALS =====}

DRAWTEXT(BUY_SIGNAL>0,L-20,'B'),COLORLIGREEN;

DRAWTEXT(SELL_SIGNAL>0,H+20,'S'),COLORLIRED;

{===== BACKTEST REFERENCE =====}

ZERO_SIGNAL:0,NODRAW;


This follows the original MNQ MS breakout logic and avoids future-looking drawing functions such as `REFX` and `BACKSET`. The swing itself is confirmed two candles later; signals are evaluated on the breakout bar. Execution must occur only once that bar's close is known.

## 1. Backtest speed: 0×, 1×, 2×, 5×, 10×

Those controls ordinarily determine **how quickly the historical simulation plays back**, not how well the strategy performs.

| Speed | What it means |
|---|---|
| 0× | Paused |
| 1× | Normal playback |
| 2× | Faster playback |
| 5× | Much faster |
| 10× | Fastest listed playback |
| Default | Platform's standard speed |

For the same strategy, historical candles, capital, and execution settings, 1× and 10× should produce the same trades and final statistics.

## 2. What the backtest is actually doing

Imagine that, on April 16, 2026, you had started with $50,000 and followed the rules in our MNQSCALP indicator.

Moomoo goes through historical price data and evaluates the strategy conditions. When a Buy condition occurs, it simulates an order. When a Sell condition occurs, it simulates an exit according to its order rules.

The result is a hypothetical trading history.

**It does not mean you would necessarily have made exactly that amount in real trading.** Real fills, slippage, commissions, order delays, and your own discretionary decisions can change the outcome.

### Understanding the backtest panels

| Panel | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| **Positions** | Simulated contracts currently held in the replay |
| **History** | Orders or transactions that the simulation has recorded |
| **Trading Asset / Trending Asset** | Usually a chart of simulated account or asset value over time; exact meaning depends on the panel label |
| **P&L** | Profit and loss generated by the simulated strategy |
| **Maximum Drawdown** | Largest peak-to-trough decline in simulated account equity |
| **Win Rate** | Percentage of completed trades classified as profitable |

Pay particular attention to **unrealized P&L**. If the test finishes with an open position, the displayed account profit may include gains or losses from a trade that has not closed.

For MNQ specifically, one index point is worth $2 per contract. With two contracts:

- 10 points in your favor = $40 gross profit.
- 10 points against you = $40 gross loss.

But that applies only while holding both contracts.

## 3. Will MNQSCALP give you live Buy/Sell signals tomorrow?

**Yes, the indicator can display Buy and Sell signals on a live MNQ chart**, provided it's applied to that chart and receiving updated market data.

Remember these two lines in our code:

```text
DRAWTEXT(BUY_SIGNAL>0,L-20,'B'),COLORLIGREEN;
DRAWTEXT(SELL_SIGNAL>0,H+20,'S'),COLORLIRED;
```

These display:


  
    B
    **Bullish structure break**
    Potential Buy signal
  
  
    S
    **Bearish structure break**
    Potential Sell signal
  


There are three important distinctions.

**First — Live signals can change before a candle closes.** Our formula evaluates the current 5-minute candle's closing price. While that candle is forming, price can briefly cross a structure level and then move back. A B or S appearing during that candle is therefore not necessarily confirmed.

For reliable signals, wait until the 5-minute candle has closed.

**Second — A Sell signal does not necessarily mean an instruction to open a short.** In our current simple backtest configuration, Sell is primarily used to exit a long position. We'll build proper long and short entries separately.

**Third — The indicator does not automatically execute trades.** It draws chart labels. If you want notifications when its conditions are met, moomoo documents a way to use custom indicators in its Algo Strategy alert workflow. <Cite ref="turn998797search0"/>

And one additional distinction: moomoo's Algo backtester may simulate intraminute ticks from one-minute OHLC data rather than historical exchange ticks. That makes historical fills approximations, particularly for fast scalps. <Cite ref="turn998797search1"/>

You mentioned that when trading activity is low, the performance rises, then when volume increases you notice large jumps or changes.

**Open positions:** Our current strategy has no stop-loss, take-profit, or mandatory end-of-day exit. It might hold two MNQ contracts for hours or even days. That means market movements keep changing the account's unrealized P&L.

**Chart display:** If you're watching the Trading Asset/equity curve, the jumps may reflect changes in the value of open positions rather than profits from newly completed trades.

**Futures contract characteristics:** The December contract's liquidity and trading activity can change over the historical period, especially as its expiration approaches.

And one correction: **high volume doesn't automatically cause a strategy to lose money.** The direction and size of the price movement relative to the open position matter much more.

{ MNQSCALP V2.1                     }
{ MNQ 5 MINUTE CHART                }
{ BREAKOUT RETEST CONFIRMATION      }
{ LONG SHORT VIRTUAL SIGNALS        }

{===== PARAMETERS =====}

RETEST_TOL:=10;

{===== CONFIRMED SWING HIGHS =====}

PH:=REF(H,3)>REF(H,4) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,5) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,2) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,1);

{===== CONFIRMED SWING LOWS =====}

PL:=REF(L,3)<REF(L,4) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,5) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,2) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,1);

{===== MARKET STRUCTURE LEVELS =====}

HIGH_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PH,REF(H,3));

LOW_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PL,REF(L,3));

{===== PREVIOUS CLOSED CANDLE BREAKS =====}

UP_RAW:=REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1)>0 AND REF(C,1)>REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1);

DN_RAW:=REF(LOW_LEVEL,1)>0 AND REF(C,1)<REF(LOW_LEVEL,1);

{===== FIRST BREAK PER SWING =====}

HAGE:=BARSLAST(REF(PH,1))+1;

LAGE:=BARSLAST(REF(PL,1))+1;

UP_FIRST:=UP_RAW AND COUNT(REF(C,1)>REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1),HAGE)=1;

DN_FIRST:=DN_RAW AND COUNT(REF(C,1)<REF(LOW_LEVEL,1),LAGE)=1;

{===== BREAKOUT SESSION =====}

BREAK_SESSION:=REF(TIME,1)>=930 AND REF(TIME,1)<1130;

BR_UP:=UP_FIRST AND BREAK_SESSION;

BR_DN:=DN_FIRST AND BREAK_SESSION;

{===== FREEZE BROKEN LEVELS =====}

UP_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_UP,REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1));

DN_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_DN,REF(LOW_LEVEL,1));

{===== TIME SINCE BREAKOUT =====}

UP_AGE:=BARSLAST(BR_UP);

DN_AGE:=BARSLAST(BR_DN);

{===== MOST RECENT BREAK DIRECTION =====}

LAST_DIR:=VALUEWHEN(BR_UP OR BR_DN,IF(BR_UP,1,-1));

{===== RETEST WINDOW =====}

UP_WINDOW:=LAST_DIR=1 AND UP_AGE>=1 AND UP_AGE<=3;

DN_WINDOW:=LAST_DIR=-1 AND DN_AGE>=1 AND DN_AGE<=3;

{===== CONFIRMATION CANDLE =====}

RANGE1:=REF(H-L,1);

BULL_CANDLE:=RANGE1>0 AND REF(C,1)>REF(O,1) AND REF(C-L,1)>=RANGE1*0.60;

BEAR_CANDLE:=RANGE1>0 AND REF(C,1)<REF(O,1) AND REF(H-C,1)>=RANGE1*0.60;

{===== LONG RETEST CONFIRMATION =====}

UP_TOUCH:=REF(L,1)<=UP_LEVEL+RETEST_TOL AND REF(L,1)>=UP_LEVEL-RETEST_TOL;

UP_RECLAIM:=REF(C,1)>UP_LEVEL;

UP_INVALID:=REF(C,1)<UP_LEVEL-RETEST_TOL;

UP_CONFIRM:=UP_WINDOW AND UP_TOUCH AND UP_RECLAIM AND BULL_CANDLE AND COUNT(UP_INVALID,MAX(UP_AGE,1))=0;

{===== SHORT RETEST CONFIRMATION =====}

DN_TOUCH:=REF(H,1)>=DN_LEVEL-RETEST_TOL AND REF(H,1)<=DN_LEVEL+RETEST_TOL;

DN_REJECT:=REF(C,1)<DN_LEVEL;

DN_INVALID:=REF(C,1)>DN_LEVEL+RETEST_TOL;

DN_CONFIRM:=DN_WINDOW AND DN_TOUCH AND DN_REJECT AND BEAR_CANDLE AND COUNT(DN_INVALID,MAX(DN_AGE,1))=0;

{===== ONLY ONE ENTRY PER BREAKOUT =====}

UP_ENTRY_RAW:=UP_CONFIRM AND COUNT(UP_CONFIRM,MAX(UP_AGE,1))=1;

DN_ENTRY_RAW:=DN_CONFIRM AND COUNT(DN_CONFIRM,MAX(DN_AGE,1))=1;

{===== NEW YORK ENTRY HOURS =====}

SESSION_OK:=TIME>=935 AND TIME<1130;

{===== SESSION CUTOFF =====}

FLAT_NOW:=TIME>=1155 AND REF(TIME,1)<1155;

{===== RAW ENTRY CANDIDATES =====}

RAW_LI:=UP_ENTRY_RAW AND SESSION_OK;

RAW_SI:=DN_ENTRY_RAW AND SESSION_OK;

{===== VIRTUAL LONG STATE =====}

LONG_MODE:=VALUEWHEN(RAW_LI OR DN_FIRST OR FLAT_NOW,IF(RAW_LI AND NOT(FLAT_NOW),1,0));

{===== VIRTUAL SHORT STATE =====}

SHORT_MODE:=VALUEWHEN(RAW_SI OR UP_FIRST OR FLAT_NOW,IF(RAW_SI AND NOT(FLAT_NOW),1,0));

HAD_LONG:=REF(LONG_MODE,1)=1;

HAD_SHORT:=REF(SHORT_MODE,1)=1;

{===== ENTRY SIGNALS =====}

LI_SIG:=RAW_LI AND NOT(HAD_LONG) AND NOT(HAD_SHORT);

SI_SIG:=RAW_SI AND NOT(HAD_SHORT) AND NOT(HAD_LONG);

{===== STRUCTURE EXIT SIGNALS =====}

EL_SIG:=DN_FIRST AND HAD_LONG;

ES_SIG:=UP_FIRST AND HAD_SHORT;

FN_SIG:=FLAT_NOW;

{===== NUMERICAL OUTPUTS =====}

LONG_ENTRY:IF(LI_SIG,1,0),NODRAW;

SHORT_ENTRY:IF(SI_SIG,1,0),NODRAW;

PL:=REF(L,3)<REF(L,4) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,5) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,2) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,1);

{===== MARKET STRUCTURE LEVELS =====}

HIGH_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PH,REF(H,3));

LOW_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PL,REF(L,3));

{===== CLOSED CANDLE BREAKS =====}

UP_RAW:=REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1)>0 AND REF(C,1)>REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1);

DN_RAW:=REF(LOW_LEVEL,1)>0 AND REF(C,1)<REF(LOW_LEVEL,1);

{===== FIRST BREAK PER SWING =====}

HAGE:=BARSLAST(REF(PH,1))+1;

LAGE:=BARSLAST(REF(PL,1))+1;

UP_FIRST:=UP_RAW AND COUNT(REF(C,1)>REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1),HAGE)=1;

DN_FIRST:=DN_RAW AND COUNT(REF(C,1)<REF(LOW_LEVEL,1),LAGE)=1;

{===== BREAKOUT SESSION =====}

BREAK_SESSION:=REF(TIME,1)>=930 AND REF(TIME,1)<1130;

BR_UP:=UP_FIRST AND BREAK_SESSION;

BR_DN:=DN_FIRST AND BREAK_SESSION;

{===== FREEZE BREAKOUT LEVELS =====}

UP_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_UP,REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1));

DN_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_DN,REF(LOW_LEVEL,1));

{===== VOLATILITY BASED RETEST ZONE =====}

AVG_RANGE:=REF(MA(H-L,14),1);

UP_TOL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_UP,MAX(10,AVG_RANGE*0.75));

DN_TOL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_DN,MAX(10,AVG_RANGE*0.75));

{===== BREAKOUT AGE =====}

UP_AGE:=BARSLAST(BR_UP);

DN_AGE:=BARSLAST(BR_DN);

{===== LAST BREAK DIRECTION =====}

LAST_DIR:=VALUEWHEN(BR_UP OR BR_DN,IF(BR_UP,1,-1));

{===== RETEST WINDOWS =====}

UP_WINDOW:=LAST_DIR=1 AND UP_AGE>=1 AND UP_AGE<=RETEST_BARS;

DN_WINDOW:=LAST_DIR=-1 AND DN_AGE>=1 AND DN_AGE<=RETEST_BARS;

{===== CONFIRMATION CANDLE =====}

RANGE1:=REF(H-L,1);

BULL_CANDLE:=RANGE1>0 AND REF(C,1)>REF(O,1) AND REF(C-L,1)>=RANGE1*0.50;

BEAR_CANDLE:=RANGE1>0 AND REF(C,1)<REF(O,1) AND REF(H-C,1)>=RANGE1*0.50;

{===== BULLISH RETEST =====}

UP_TOUCH:=REF(L,1)<=UP_LEVEL+UP_TOL AND REF(H,1)>=UP_LEVEL-UP_TOL;

UP_RECLAIM:=REF(C,1)>UP_LEVEL;

UP_INVALID:=REF(C,1)<UP_LEVEL-UP_TOL;

UP_CONFIRM:=UP_WINDOW AND UP_TOUCH AND UP_RECLAIM AND BULL_CANDLE AND COUNT(UP_INVALID,MAX(UP_AGE,1))=0;

{===== BEARISH RETEST =====}

DN_INVALID:=REF(C,1)>DN_LEVEL+DN_TOL;

DN_ENTRY_RAW:=DN_CONFIRM AND COUNT(DN_CONFIRM,MAX(DN_AGE,1))=1;

SESSION_OK:=TIME>=935 AND TIME<1130;

{===== FLAT TIME =====}

RAW_SI:=DN_ENTRY_RAW AND SESSION_OK;

{===== VIRTUAL POSITION STATE =====}

SHORT_MODE:=VALUEWHEN(RAW_SI OR UP_FIRST OR FLAT_NOW,IF(RAW_SI AND NOT(FLAT_NOW),1,0));

HAD_LONG:=REF(LONG_MODE,1)=1;

HAD_SHORT:=REF(SHORT_MODE,1)=1;

{===== ENTRIES =====}

LI_SIG:=RAW_LI AND NOT(HAD_LONG) AND NOT(HAD_SHORT);

SI_SIG:=RAW_SI AND NOT(HAD_SHORT) AND NOT(HAD_LONG);

{===== EXITS =====}

EL_SIG:=DN_FIRST AND HAD_LONG;

ES_SIG:=UP_FIRST AND HAD_SHORT;

FN_SIG:=FLAT_NOW;

{===== NUMERICAL OUTPUTS =====}

LONG_ENTRY:IF(LI_SIG,1,0),NODRAW;

SHORT_ENTRY:IF(SI_SIG,1,0),NODRAW;

LONG_EXIT:IF(EL_SIG OR (FN_SIG AND HAD_LONG),1,0),NODRAW;

SHORT_EXIT:IF(ES_SIG OR (FN_SIG AND HAD_SHORT),1,0),NODRAW;

{===== BASIC BACKTEST OUTPUTS =====}

BUY_SIGNAL:IF(LI_SIG,1,0),NODRAW;

SELL_SIGNAL:IF(EL_SIG OR (FN_SIG AND HAD_LONG),1,0),NODRAW;

{===== BULLISH BREAKOUT SETUP =====}

DRAWTEXT(BR_UP,L-45,'BU'),COLOR66BB99;

{===== BEARISH BREAKOUT SETUP =====}

DRAWTEXT(BR_DN,H+45,'BD'),COLORCC8888;

{===== LONG ENTRY =====}

{===== SHORT ENTRY =====}

{===== SESSION CUTOFF =====}

DRAWTEXT(FN_SIG,H+60,'FN'),COLORFFFFFF;

The 14-bar average candle range is a volatility proxy, not ATR. Its purpose here is to create a retest zone that adapts to MNQ's recent 5-minute price movement. The exact formula hasn't been compilation-tested in your editor, although it uses functions already familiar from the working indicators.

## How to interpret the new chart


  | Label | Meaning | Trade action |
  |---|---|---|
  | BU | Bullish breakout detected | Wait for retest |
  | BD | Bearish breakout detected | Wait for retest |
  | LI | Bullish retest confirmed | Long entry candidate |
  | SI | Bearish retest confirmed | Short entry candidate |
  | EL | Opposing bearish break | Virtual long exit |
  | ES | Opposing bullish break | Virtual short exit |
  | **FN** | Session cutoff | Flattening reminder |


A breakout label should appear before its corresponding entry label. For example, **BD → pullback → bearish confirmation → SI**.

BU/BD identify the bar immediately after the confirmed breakout candle. LI/SI identify the bar immediately after the confirmation candle. This lets us use closed-candle information instead of assuming a developing candle is final.

EL/ES still represent virtual structure-based exits. They do not yet include an actual protective stop, TP1, or runner exit, and FN does not execute an order by itself.

## Step 3 — Full MNQSCALP V2.4 code

This version adds a second pullback pattern while keeping your existing breakout-level retest. It also replaces the previous virtual position-state logic with a more consistent event-history approach.

Both patterns still require candle confirmation. Neither uses future-looking `REFX` or `BACKSET`.


{====================================}
{ MNQSCALP V2.4                     }
{ MNQ 5 MINUTE CHART                }
{ ALL HOURS                         }
{ BREAKOUT RETEST OR PULLBACK       }
{ CLOSED CANDLE CONFIRMATION        }
{ VIRTUAL POSITION STATE           }
{====================================}

{===== PARAMETERS =====}

RETEST_BARS:=8;

{===== CONFIRMED SWINGS =====}

PH:=REF(H,3)>REF(H,4) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,5) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,2) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,1);

PL:=REF(L,3)<REF(L,4) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,5) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,2) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,1);

{===== STRUCTURE LEVELS =====}

HIGH_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PH,REF(H,3));

LOW_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PL,REF(L,3));

{===== BREAKOUT DETECTION =====}

UP_RAW:=REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1)>0 AND REF(C,1)>REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1);

DN_RAW:=REF(LOW_LEVEL,1)>0 AND REF(C,1)<REF(LOW_LEVEL,1);

HAGE:=BARSLAST(REF(PH,1))+1;

LAGE:=BARSLAST(REF(PL,1))+1;

UP_FIRST:=UP_RAW AND COUNT(REF(C,1)>REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1),HAGE)=1;

DN_FIRST:=DN_RAW AND COUNT(REF(C,1)<REF(LOW_LEVEL,1),LAGE)=1;

{===== ALL HOURS BREAKOUTS =====}

BR_UP:=UP_FIRST;

BR_DN:=DN_FIRST;

{===== FREEZE BREAKOUT LEVELS =====}

UP_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_UP,REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1));

DN_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_DN,REF(LOW_LEVEL,1));

{===== RETEST TOLERANCE =====}

AVG_RANGE:=REF(MA(H-L,14),1);

UP_TOL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_UP,MAX(10,AVG_RANGE*0.75));

DN_TOL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_DN,MAX(10,AVG_RANGE*0.75));

{===== BREAKOUT AGE =====}

UP_AGE:=BARSLAST(BR_UP);

DN_AGE:=BARSLAST(BR_DN);

LAST_DIR:=VALUEWHEN(BR_UP OR BR_DN,IF(BR_UP,1,-1));

UP_WINDOW:=LAST_DIR=1 AND UP_AGE>=1 AND UP_AGE<=RETEST_BARS;

DN_WINDOW:=LAST_DIR=-1 AND DN_AGE>=1 AND DN_AGE<=RETEST_BARS;

{===== CLOSED CANDLE STRENGTH =====}

RANGE1:=REF(H-L,1);

BULL_CANDLE:=RANGE1>0 AND REF(C,1)>REF(O,1) AND REF(C-L,1)>=RANGE1*0.50;

BEAR_CANDLE:=RANGE1>0 AND REF(C,1)<REF(O,1) AND REF(H-C,1)>=RANGE1*0.50;

{===== ORIGINAL LEVEL RETEST =====}

UP_TOUCH:=REF(L,1)<=UP_LEVEL+UP_TOL AND REF(H,1)>=UP_LEVEL-UP_TOL;

DN_TOUCH:=REF(H,1)>=DN_LEVEL-DN_TOL AND REF(L,1)<=DN_LEVEL+DN_TOL;

UP_RETEST:=UP_WINDOW AND UP_TOUCH AND REF(C,1)>UP_LEVEL AND BULL_CANDLE;

DN_RETEST:=DN_WINDOW AND DN_TOUCH AND REF(C,1)<DN_LEVEL AND BEAR_CANDLE;

{===== STRUCTURAL PULLBACK =====}
{COUNTERTREND CANDLE THEN CONTINUATION}

UP_PULLBACK:=UP_WINDOW AND UP_AGE>=2 AND REF(C,2)<REF(O,2) AND REF(C,1)>REF(H,2) AND REF(C,1)>UP_LEVEL AND BULL_CANDLE;

DN_PULLBACK:=DN_WINDOW AND DN_AGE>=2 AND REF(C,2)>REF(O,2) AND REF(C,1)<REF(L,2) AND REF(C,1)<DN_LEVEL AND BEAR_CANDLE;

{===== FAILED BREAKOUTS =====}

UP_INVALID:=REF(C,1)<UP_LEVEL-UP_TOL;

DN_INVALID:=REF(C,1)>DN_LEVEL+DN_TOL;

{===== VALID CONFIRMATIONS =====}

UP_VALID:=UP_WINDOW AND (UP_RETEST OR UP_PULLBACK) AND COUNT(UP_INVALID,MAX(UP_AGE,1))=0;

DN_VALID:=DN_WINDOW AND (DN_RETEST OR DN_PULLBACK) AND COUNT(DN_INVALID,MAX(DN_AGE,1))=0;

{===== ONE ENTRY CANDIDATE PER BREAK =====}

UP_ENTRY_RAW:=UP_VALID AND COUNT(UP_VALID,MAX(UP_AGE,1))=1;

DN_ENTRY_RAW:=DN_VALID AND COUNT(DN_VALID,MAX(DN_AGE,1))=1;

{===== DIRECTIONAL CANDIDATES =====}

RAW_LI:=UP_ENTRY_RAW;

RAW_SI:=DN_ENTRY_RAW;

{===== EVENT HISTORY =====}

SEEN_LI:=COUNT(RAW_LI,0)>0;

SEEN_SI:=COUNT(RAW_SI,0)>0;

SEEN_DN:=COUNT(DN_FIRST,0)>0;

SEEN_UP:=COUNT(UP_FIRST,0)>0;

{===== VIRTUAL POSITION STATUS =====}
{LAST ENTRY MUST BE AFTER OPPOSITE EVENTS}

ACTIVE_LONG:=SEEN_LI AND (NOT(SEEN_SI) OR BARSLAST(RAW_LI)<BARSLAST(RAW_SI)) AND (NOT(SEEN_DN) OR BARSLAST(RAW_LI)<BARSLAST(DN_FIRST));

ACTIVE_SHORT:=SEEN_SI AND (NOT(SEEN_LI) OR BARSLAST(RAW_SI)<BARSLAST(RAW_LI)) AND (NOT(SEEN_UP) OR BARSLAST(RAW_SI)<BARSLAST(UP_FIRST));

HAD_LONG:=REF(ACTIVE_LONG,1);

HAD_SHORT:=REF(ACTIVE_SHORT,1);

{===== ENTRY SIGNALS =====}

LI_SIG:=RAW_LI AND NOT(HAD_LONG) AND NOT(HAD_SHORT);

SI_SIG:=RAW_SI AND NOT(HAD_SHORT) AND NOT(HAD_LONG);

{===== STRUCTURAL EXIT SIGNALS =====}

EL_SIG:=DN_FIRST AND HAD_LONG;

ES_SIG:=UP_FIRST AND HAD_SHORT;

{===== NUMERICAL OUTPUTS =====}

LONG_ENTRY:IF(LI_SIG,1,0),NODRAW;

SHORT_ENTRY:IF(SI_SIG,1,0),NODRAW;

LONG_EXIT:IF(EL_SIG,1,0),NODRAW;

SHORT_EXIT:IF(ES_SIG,1,0),NODRAW;

{===== BASIC BACKTEST OUTPUTS =====}

BUY_SIGNAL:IF(LI_SIG,1,0),NODRAW;

SELL_SIGNAL:IF(EL_SIG,1,0),NODRAW;

{===== BREAKOUT MARKERS =====}

DRAWTEXT(BR_UP,L-45,'BU'),COLOR66BB99;

DRAWTEXT(BR_DN,H+45,'BD'),COLORCC8888;

{===== LONG ENTRY =====}

STICKLINE(LI_SIG,L-3,L-12,1,0),COLOR00FF66;

DRAWTEXT(LI_SIG,L-20,'LI'),COLOR00FF66;

{===== SHORT ENTRY =====}

STICKLINE(SI_SIG,H+3,H+12,1,0),COLORFF4040;

DRAWTEXT(SI_SIG,H+20,'SI'),COLORFF4040;

{===== LONG EXIT =====}

STICKLINE(EL_SIG,L-3,L-12,1,0),COLORFFFF00;

DRAWTEXT(EL_SIG,L-35,'EL'),COLORFFFF00;

{===== SHORT EXIT =====}

STICKLINE(ES_SIG,H+3,H+12,1,0),COLOR00FFFF;

DRAWTEXT(ES_SIG,H+35,'ES'),COLOR00FFFF;

{===== REFERENCE =====}

ZERO_SIGNAL:0,NODRAW;

{====================================}

{===== PARAMETERS =====}

RETEST_BARS:=8;

{===== CONFIRMED SWINGS =====}

PH:=REF(H,3)>REF(H,4) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,5) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,2) AND REF(H,3)>REF(H,1);

PL:=REF(L,3)<REF(L,4) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,5) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,2) AND REF(L,3)<REF(L,1);

{===== MARKET STRUCTURE LEVELS =====}

HIGH_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PH,REF(H,3));

LOW_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(PL,REF(L,3));

{===== COMPLETED CANDLE BREAKS =====}

UP_RAW:=REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1)>0 AND REF(C,1)>REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1);

DN_RAW:=REF(LOW_LEVEL,1)>0 AND REF(C,1)<REF(LOW_LEVEL,1);

{===== FIRST BREAK PER SWING =====}

HAGE:=BARSLAST(REF(PH,1))+1;

LAGE:=BARSLAST(REF(PL,1))+1;

UP_FIRST:=UP_RAW AND COUNT(REF(C,1)>REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1),HAGE)=1;

DN_FIRST:=DN_RAW AND COUNT(REF(C,1)<REF(LOW_LEVEL,1),LAGE)=1;

{===== ALL HOURS STRUCTURE DETECTION =====}

BR_UP:=UP_FIRST;

BR_DN:=DN_FIRST;

{===== FREEZE BREAKOUT LEVELS =====}

UP_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_UP,REF(HIGH_LEVEL,1));

DN_LEVEL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_DN,REF(LOW_LEVEL,1));

{===== VOLATILITY BASED RETEST ZONE =====}

AVG_RANGE:=REF(MA(H-L,14),1);

UP_TOL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_UP,MAX(10,AVG_RANGE*0.75));

DN_TOL:=VALUEWHEN(BR_DN,MAX(10,AVG_RANGE*0.75));

{===== BREAKOUT AGE =====}

UP_AGE:=BARSLAST(BR_UP);

DN_AGE:=BARSLAST(BR_DN);

{===== LAST BREAK DIRECTION =====}

LAST_DIR:=VALUEWHEN(BR_UP OR BR_DN,IF(BR_UP,1,-1));

{===== RETEST WINDOWS =====}

UP_WINDOW:=LAST_DIR=1 AND UP_AGE>=1 AND UP_AGE<=RETEST_BARS;

DN_WINDOW:=LAST_DIR=-1 AND DN_AGE>=1 AND DN_AGE<=RETEST_BARS;

{===== CONFIRMATION CANDLE =====}

RANGE1:=REF(H-L,1);

BULL_CANDLE:=RANGE1>0 AND REF(C,1)>REF(O,1) AND REF(C-L,1)>=RANGE1*0.50;

BEAR_CANDLE:=RANGE1>0 AND REF(C,1)<REF(O,1) AND REF(H-C,1)>=RANGE1*0.50;

{===== BULLISH RETEST =====}

UP_TOUCH:=REF(L,1)<=UP_LEVEL+UP_TOL AND REF(H,1)>=UP_LEVEL-UP_TOL;

UP_RECLAIM:=REF(C,1)>UP_LEVEL;

UP_INVALID:=REF(C,1)<UP_LEVEL-UP_TOL;

UP_CONFIRM:=UP_WINDOW AND UP_TOUCH AND UP_RECLAIM AND BULL_CANDLE AND COUNT(UP_INVALID,MAX(UP_AGE,1))=0;

{===== BEARISH RETEST =====}

DN_TOUCH:=REF(H,1)>=DN_LEVEL-DN_TOL AND REF(L,1)<=DN_LEVEL+DN_TOL;

DN_REJECT:=REF(C,1)<DN_LEVEL;

DN_INVALID:=REF(C,1)>DN_LEVEL+DN_TOL;

DN_CONFIRM:=DN_WINDOW AND DN_TOUCH AND DN_REJECT AND BEAR_CANDLE AND COUNT(DN_INVALID,MAX(DN_AGE,1))=0;

{===== ONE CONFIRMATION PER BREAKOUT =====}

UP_ENTRY_RAW:=UP_CONFIRM AND COUNT(UP_CONFIRM,MAX(UP_AGE,1))=1;

DN_ENTRY_RAW:=DN_CONFIRM AND COUNT(DN_CONFIRM,MAX(DN_AGE,1))=1;

{===== DAY TRADING HOURS =====}

ENTRY_OK:=TIME>=300 AND TIME<1630;

{===== MANDATORY END OF DAY SIGNAL =====}

FLAT_NOW:=TIME>=1645 AND REF(TIME,1)<1645;

{===== FILTERED ENTRY CANDIDATES =====}

RAW_LI:=UP_ENTRY_RAW AND ENTRY_OK;

RAW_SI:=DN_ENTRY_RAW AND ENTRY_OK;

{===== VIRTUAL POSITION STATE =====}
